comparison: Both evaluate thioredoxin reductase genetic experiments (C57-C60). OpenEval finds the data supported but notes interpretability limitations. Peer reviewers are uncertain, explicitly critiquing that the authors should test lower Trr activity using weaker promoters or heterozygous diploids rather than accepting that perturbation is not possible.

Both evaluate early oxidation targets and cluster analysis (C15, C43, C51-C54). OpenEval emphasizes thioredoxin reductase as early target with bioinformatic support. Peer reviewers accept the clustering analysis showing different proteins oxidize at different time points, including early oxidized redox homeostasis proteins, without critique.

Both evaluate the sudden redox collapse observation (C1, C14, C42). OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from OxICAT measurements and temporal patterns. Peer reviewers describe this as 'intriguing' and 'convincing' with 'very thorough' analysis, accepting that oxidation reaches maximum ~24 hours before viability collapse.

Both evaluate NADPH depletion as trigger for protein oxidation (C2, C3, C16, C18, C77). OpenEval finds temporal correlation and mechanistic link supported. Peer reviewers are uncertain about causality, noting conclusions are 'somewhat limited' and requesting direct tests of whether lower NADPH levels or redox potential changes cause aging.

Both evaluate caloric restriction effects (C5, C17, C78). OpenEval finds consistent evidence of ~48 hour delays across multiple parameters. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the 'convincing' and 'very thorough' analysis without raising concerns.

Both evaluate GSH/GSSG ratios and redox potential measurements (C65-C67). OpenEval finds the biochemical measurements and Nernst equation calculations well-supported. Peer reviewers accept that oxidation increase is preceded by NADPH reduction and GSH redox potential changes without concerns.

Both evaluate oxidation reversibility (C55-C56). OpenEval finds reversibility well-supported but notes protective function (C80) is speculative. Peer reviewers accept reversibility data as part of the convincing dataset without questioning these findings.

Both evaluate ATP maintenance and viability data (C40-C41, C79). OpenEval emphasizes this contradicts starvation model and shows redox changes aren't secondary to energy failure. Peer reviewers accept that oxidation significantly precedes loss of fitness without questioning ATP or viability data.

Both evaluate oxidation of functionally important proteins (C33-C35). OpenEval notes temporal precedence before death is supported but functional consequences are inferred. Peer reviewers accept the proteome-wide analysis as part of 'very thorough' work without questioning functional category identification.

Both evaluate bioinformatic analysis of cysteine properties in clusters (C47-C50). OpenEval finds this provides mechanistic insight into early oxidation. Peer reviewers accept the analysis and request discussion of cluster F proteins (remarkably resistant), showing interest rather than rejection.

Both evaluate protective/buffering role of protein oxidation (C80, C83-C84). OpenEval rates as uncertain, noting the hypothesis is plausible but untested without direct measurements. Peer reviewers also uncertain, finding observations 'intriguing and thought-provoking' but noting limitations in drawing conclusions about oxidation's role in aging.

Both evaluate GapDH temporal measurements and water controls (C30-C31). OpenEval emphasizes GapDH as representative example and water control showing metabolism-dependence. Peer reviewers implicitly accept reversibility and hypometabolic experiments as part of convincing dataset.

Both address MES1 oxidation (C85). OpenEval rates uncertain because functional consequences weren't directly measured despite OxICAT data. Peer reviewers accept the proteome-wide analysis including specific proteins without questioning functional claims.

Partial overlap on NADPH measurements (C74-C76). OpenEval groups these with broader NADPH-oxidation causality claims. Peer reviewers accept the temporal correlation data showing NADPH reduction precedes oxidation without concerns about these specific measurements.
OpenEval evaluates comparison with RedoxDB database (C36-C37) showing overlap with known redox-sensitive proteins. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this cross-validation analysis.

OpenEval evaluates subcellular distribution analysis (C45-C46) finding no correlation except ER proteins. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers do request discussion of cluster F proteins which may relate to compartmentalization.
OpenEval evaluates literature context claims (C7-C13) about ROS and aging theories. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/context claims.
OpenEval evaluates OxICAT methodology description (C19-C21). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological background claims.
OpenEval evaluates established yeast biology context (C72-C73) about diauxic shift. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.
